findings.summary: The tests:skipped gate returned FAIL on this slice's own candidate tree, counting fixture string literals in src/skip-gate.test.ts and src/gate-policy.test.ts as newly disabled tests.
findings.evidence: Re-ran the clear condition against the live worktree with the shipped build: runSkipGate({ worktreeDir: <worktree>, featureRef: "feat-claude-code/afk-v2-acceptance-scope-gates", detectors: DEFAULT_SKIP_DETECTORS, testFileGlobs: ["**/*.test.ts"] }) now returns {"status":"PASS","failureKind":null,"detail":"No detector counts more disabled tests on this candidate than on feat-claude-code/afk-v2-acceptance-scope-gates (1 detector(s) over 529 candidate path(s))."}. The negative half was re-run in a scratch git repo outside the tree under review: a committed base with two live it("...") tests, then one rewritten to it.skip("subtracts", returns {"status":"FAIL","failureKind":"COMMAND","detail":"This candidate disables more tests than HEAD does: vitest-ts \"it\\.skip\" 0 \u2192 1. Re-enable the test, or fix what it caught."}. Fix is commit bc8bfef: src/skip-gate.ts:139-187 stripNonCode blanks comments and string/template literals (preserving line breaks) once per file in countAll (:220-227) before countPattern (:189-191) runs.
findings.expected: B-06: the gate counts each detector's patterns on the base tree and the candidate tree and fails only on an increase, so pre-existing occurrences do not fire; definition of done: it fires on a newly introduced skip or .only and not a pre-existing one.
findings.observed: The gate returns PASS on this slice's own tree, where no test is disabled, and still returns FAIL naming the detector pattern when a real it("x") is rewritten to it.skip("x").
findings.clearCondition: runSkipGate with DEFAULT_SKIP_DETECTORS, testFileGlobs ["**/*.test.ts"], this worktree and featureRef feat-claude-code/afk-v2-acceptance-scope-gates returns status PASS, while a candidate that genuinely disables a test returns status FAIL naming it.

findings.summary: src/skip-gate.ts embedded three raw U+0000 bytes as a Map-key separator, so Git classified the slice's central new module as binary: no reviewable diff and no textual merge.
findings.evidence: git diff --numstat b732ce0..HEAD -- src/skip-gate.ts now reports "362\t0\tsrc/skip-gate.ts" instead of "-\t-", and git diff b732ce0..HEAD -- src/skip-gate.ts emits a textual patch ("new file mode 100644 ... @@ -0,0 +1,362 @@" followed by the source lines). A byte scan of the file ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes) counts 0 NUL bytes and 0 control bytes other than CR/LF/TAB. The separator is now the escape KEY_SEPARATOR = "\u001f" at src/skip-gate.ts:206, and countKey (:208-210) still composes detectorId + separator + pattern, so the composite Map key keeps distinguishing detector/pattern pairs; src/skip-gate.test.ts adds an assertion that the module carries no raw control byte and that the escape is spelled out. (git show --stat bc8bfef still prints "Bin 9536 -> 12957 bytes" because the pre-fix blob was the binary side of that pair; the file as shipped at HEAD is text.)
findings.expected: src/skip-gate.ts is a TypeScript source module reviewable by git diff and mergeable by Git's text merge driver, as ARCHITECTURE.md's Gates row presents it beside src/scope-gate.ts.
findings.observed: Git treats the file as text: numeric numstat counts and a full textual patch, with the composite key semantics unchanged.
findings.clearCondition: git diff --numstat <slice-base>..HEAD -- src/skip-gate.ts reports numeric added/removed line counts instead of "-  -", and git diff emits a textual patch for the file, with the composite Map key still distinguishing detector/pattern pairs.
